newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy dropping $1.9 billion bid for NYSEG.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy dropping $1.9 billion bid for NYSEG.

text.p: Independent power producer CalEnergy Co. Inc. said on Friday it dropped its $1.9 billion bid to acquire New York State Electric & Gas Corp. due to lack of support from NYSEG shareholders.

CalEnergy said a $159 million tender offer launched to acquire 9.9 percent of NYSEG shares was undersubscribed. The tender was the first step in its effort to acquire the whole company in a transaction valued at $1.9 billion.
In a strongly worded statement, CalEnergy accused NYSEG's management of undermining its bid.
"We believe NYSEG's frivolous and unrelenting litigation efforts and misinformation campaign unfortunately resulted in the NYSEG shareholders' decision not to accept our offer," the company said.
"We intend to evaluate our options and explore other potential combinations," it added.

Minimum conditions of the tender offer, which expired at midnight, were not met, CalEnergy said. The tender offer was valued at $24.50 a share. NYSEG's stock closed above that on Thursday, at $25.25. It fell 87.5 cents to $24.375 in early consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange Friday..

NYSEG had urged holders not to tender their shares and refused to sit down at the negotiating table, saying that the offer did not reflect the value of the company. CalEnergy launched its bid July 15, saying it would be willing to pay $27.50 a share in a negotiated transaction.
Earlier this week, CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol said he would drop the effort if did not get enough shareholder support.
Industry analysts said CalEnergy was expected to rebound quickly from the failed effort and had plenty of opportunities to acquire another utility.
"I think the company has demonstrated they are disciplined acquirers," said Ali Agha of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
CalEnergy rose 37.5 cents to $35.75, also on the NYSE.
